extracted.intended_audience: K–12 teachers, literacy coaches, education researchers, and policymakers interested in writing instruction and assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evidence about implementing and evaluating the 6+1 Trait Writing model in K–12 classrooms, including the seven writing traits, instructional strategies, use of rubrics for formative assessment, and standards for rigorous evaluation of effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas are the main message, the content of the piece, the theme, together with the details that enrich and develop that theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the central message and supporting details separately from organization or mechanics. Example contrast: an essay may have interesting, innovative ideas but be poorly organized; trait-based rubrics allow targeted feedback to build this trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization is the internal structure, the thread of central meaning, the logical and sometimes intriguing pattern of the ideas within a piece of writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the logical flow and structure that connects ideas. Use rubric descriptors to identify strengths/weaknesses in sequencing, transitions, and coherence so students can revise for clearer structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice is the heart and soul, the magic and conviction of the individual writer coming out through the words — the feeling, the wit, along with the sense of an individual perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the authenticity, engagement, and appropriateness of the writer's voice for audience and purpose. Use trait feedback to encourage expressive, purposeful tone rather than generic or flat prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Choice (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word choice is the use of rich, colorful, precise language that moves and enlightens the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the specificity, vividness, and appropriateness of vocabulary. Rubric-based feedback can point to places to substitute precise words or remove vague phrasing to strengthen meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Fluency (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence fluency is the rhythm and flow of the language, the sound of word patterns, the way in which the writing plays to the ear and not just to the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate variety of sentence structures, smoothness, and readability aloud. Use sentence-combining and fluency exercises tied to rubric descriptors to improve this trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions refer to the mechanics of writing: spelling, grammar and usage, punctuation, capitalization, paragraph formatting, and related mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess correctness and consistency of standard usage. Provide targeted editing and proofreading strategies based on rubric levels rather than treating mechanics as the only focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (+1) (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation zeros in on the form and layout of the text and its readability; the piece should be pleasing to the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider formatting, layout, and visual presentation especially when publication or presentation is an expected outcome. Note: the '+1' presentation trait is optional in some settings and may not be appropriate for all classrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching the language of rubrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach students the language of rubrics for writing assessment so they understand trait descriptors and can use them to self- and peer-assess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction on rubric vocabulary helps students interpret feedback and set revision goals; include modeling, practice, and justification activities where students explain scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading and scoring papers (including student scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have students and teachers read and score papers, justify the scores, and have students do so themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use guided practice in scoring and justification to deepen understanding of criteria; peer- and self-scoring supports formative assessment and metacognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching focused revision strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach focused revision strategies that target specific traits and help students improve their writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted revision exercises aligned to rubric traits (e.g., revise for stronger organization or more precise word choice) rather than generic 'rewrite' directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling participation in the writing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Model teacher participation in the writing process, demonstrating planning, drafting, and revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should model their own writing and revision decisions using trait language so students see how trait-based feedback informs changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Having students read and analyze models
rubrics_metrics.description: Have students read and analyze materials that demonstrate varying writing quality using the trait framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exemplar texts and anchor papers to show different rubric levels for each trait; analysis helps students internalize quality indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving students effective prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Give students writing assignments to respond to effective prompts (prompts that are engaging and provide adequate structure, guidance, and context to elicit detailed responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design prompts that align with intended traits and provide enough scaffolding so students can produce work on which trait feedback is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaving writing lessons into other subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave writing lessons into other subjects, integrating trait instruction across content areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the traits framework in content instruction so students practice discipline-specific writing (e.g., science explanations, history arguments) with trait-aligned goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching students to set goals and monitor progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach students to set writing goals and monitor their progress toward those goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rubrics to help students set specific, measurable revision goals and track improvements over time (formative assessment cycles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating learning goals for writing into curriculum planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate learning goals for writing into curriculum planning at the unit and school level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align rubric-based trait targets with curriculum objectives so writing instruction is coherent across lessons and grade levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching ways to structure nonfiction writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach methods to structure nonfiction writing so students can plan and organize informational and expository texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit structures (e.g., introductions, topic sentences, evidence integration) linked to organization and ideas traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rubrics for formative assessment (self-, peer-, teacher-scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing use of rubrics to provide feedback through self-scoring, peer scoring, and teacher scoring at various stages of the writing process (planning, drafting, revision, redrafting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubrics support formative assessment cycles; incorporate self- and peer-assessment opportunities and teach students to use rubric criteria to guide revision. Correlational evidence links higher trait scores to better performance on some standardized assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic versus analytic scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Holistic scoring assigns a single overall score for writing quality; analytic (trait-based) scoring rates multiple distinct traits (ideas, organization, voice, word choice, sentence fluency, conventions, presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study used holistic scores for confirmatory analysis and trait scores for exploratory analyses. Use holistic scoring for overall judgments and analytic trait scores for diagnostic, formative feedback and targeted instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedures to prevent bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational procedures to limit bias in scoring: raters and research staff were blinded to pre/post status and treatment/control assignment; research and professional development teams operated independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement rater blinding, separate operational teams, and rater training to reduce intentional or unintentional bias during essay scoring. Document these methods in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation fidelity measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of implementation focused on teacher self-report surveys about classroom practices (use of recommended strategies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-report surveys can provide relative information about implementation differences between groups but are subject to bias and may not indicate magnitude or exact levels of classroom implementation; observational validation is recommended when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and analytic standards for evidence of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark standards for evaluating effectiveness included randomized assignment (clustered by school), baseline pretest measurement, controls for school poverty level and teacher-reported baseline characteristics, accounting for clustering of students within schools, pre-specified analysis plans, and handling of missing outcome data (imputation and alternative deletion approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate multilevel models that adjust for baseline differences and clustering; pre-specify primary analyses; report sensitivity checks (e.g., excluding missing cases, alternative model specifications) and effect sizes (e.g., standardized differences) along with p-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of effective adolescent writing instruction (correspondence to Writing Next)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core instructional elements supported by meta-analysis and incorporated into 6+1 Trait activities include: having students analyze models of good writing; explicitly teaching strategies for planning, revising, and editing; involving students in collaborative use of strategies; assigning specific product goals; using sentence combining; prewriting and inquiry activities; integrating writing with content instruction; encouraging use of technology for development/publication; and teaching study of models and process approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align classroom activities and trait-based rubrics with empirically supported practices (as summarized in Writing Next) to increase likelihood of positive effects on adolescent writing.
